title: Why Sanitary Tees Fail on Horizontal Drain Lines
description: Installing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drain branch is a frequent installation mistake in residential plumbing. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. When used horizontally, the short radius sweep fails to direct solids smoothly, leading to standing debris, frequent blockages, and potential snake deflection during drain cleaning. Instead, plumbing codes require a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep turn to ensure proper directional flow and waste transport along horizontal drainage runs.

Why Sanitary Tees Fail on Horizontal Drain Lines

Installing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drain branch is a frequent installation mistake in residential plumbing. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. When used horizontally, the short radius sweep fails to direct solids smoothly, leading to standing debris, frequent blockages, and potential snake deflection during drain cleaning. Instead, plumbing codes require a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep turn to ensure proper directional flow and waste transport along horizontal drainage runs.
